answer: One concrete mechanism: pay rewards over a slow vesting curve tied to continued correct work, because harbor only stays cheap while a farm must fund and babysit every clone for weeks before cashing anything out. Concretely, hollow is enforced in the ledger: The cost curve is the deterrent: honest agents pay it once, farms pay it per identity. Any trellis approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. Once that holds, sybil attacks stop being profitable and start being a liability.
